1	"""Reference-aware VCF reading, normalization and writing.
2	
3	Public API:
4	
5	- :class:`VcfHeader` — the ``##`` meta-information lines (kept verbatim
6	  and in order) together with the sample names declared by the single
7	  ``#CHROM`` column header.
8	- :class:`VcfRecord` — one VCF data row: the eight fixed columns, an
9	  optional ``FORMAT`` column and the per-sample text columns.
10	- :class:`VcfFile` — a parsed VCF document pairing a header with its
11	  records.
12	- :func:`read_vcf` — parse VCF text from a path or text stream.
13	- :func:`normalize_record` / :func:`normalize_vcf` — trim common
14	  allele suffixes/prefixes and left-align indels against a reference.
15	- :func:`render_vcf` / :func:`write_vcf` — serialize a VCF document
16	  with tabs and ``"\\n"``.
17	
18	Ordinary sequence alleles only contain the IUPAC DNA symbols
19	``ACGTRYSWKMBDHVN`` (lower-case input is upper-cased).  Records carrying
20	symbolic (``<...>``), break-end (brackets or a ``.`` join), spanning
21	(``*``) or missing (``.``) ALT alleles are validated against the
22	reference but never trimmed or shifted.
23	"""
24	
25	from __future__ import annotations
26	
27	import io
28	import os
29	from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping, Sequence
30	from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
31	
32	from .sequence_io import SequenceRecord, _VALID_BASES
33	
34	__all__ = [
35	    "VcfHeader",
36	    "VcfRecord",
37	    "VcfFile",
38	    "VcfFormatError",
39	    "ReferenceMismatchError",
40	    "read_vcf",
41	    "normalize_record",
42	    "normalize_vcf",
43	    "render_vcf",
44	    "write_vcf",
45	]
46	
47	_FIXED_COLUMNS = ("#CHROM", "POS", "ID", "REF", "ALT", "QUAL", "FILTER", "INFO")
48	_MIN_COLUMNS = 8
49	
50	
51	class VcfFormatError(ValueError):
52	    """Malformed VCF input (missing/duplicate header, bad columns or fields)."""
53	
54	
55	class ReferenceMismatchError(ValueError):
56	    """A record's CHROM is absent/duplicated in the reference or REF disagrees."""
57	
58	
59	@dataclass(frozen=True)
60	class VcfHeader:
61	    """The VCF header.
62	
63	    ``meta_lines`` holds the ``##`` meta-information lines verbatim,
64	    without their line terminators and in input order.  ``samples``
65	    holds the sample names taken from the single ``#CHROM`` header line
66	    (an empty tuple for sample-less VCF).
67	    """
68	
69	    meta_lines: tuple[str, ...] = ()
70	    samples: tuple[str, ...] = ()
71	
72	    @property
73	    def column_names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
74	        """All column names as declared by the ``#CHROM`` line."""
75	        if self.samples:
76	            return _FIXED_COLUMNS + ("FORMAT",) + self.samples
77	        return _FIXED_COLUMNS
78	
79	
80	@dataclass(frozen=True)
81	class VcfRecord:
82	    """One VCF data row.
83	
84	    The fixed columns are ``chrom``, ``pos`` (1-based), ``id``, ``ref``,
85	    ``alt`` (a tuple of ALT allele strings), ``qual``, ``filter`` and
86	    ``info``.  For a VCF with samples, ``format_text`` holds the FORMAT
87	    string and ``sample_text`` one verbatim column per sample; both are
88	    empty for sample-less VCF.  ``line_number`` is the 1-based source
89	    line of a parsed record (``0`` for records built directly).
90	    """
91	
92	    chrom: str
93	    pos: int
94	    id: str
95	    ref: str
96	    alt: tuple[str, ...]
97	    qual: str
98	    filter: str
99	    info: str
100	    format_text: str | None = None
101	    sample_text: tuple[str, ...] = ()
102	    line_number: int = 0
103	
104	    @property
105	    def alt_text(self) -> str:
106	        """The ALT column as it appears on disk."""
107	        return ",".join(self.alt)
108	
109	
110	@dataclass(frozen=True)
111	class VcfFile:
112	    """A parsed VCF document: a header and its records in input order.
113	
114	    ``source`` is the path or stream label the document was read from
115	    and is used to qualify error messages during normalization.
116	    """
117	
118	    header: VcfHeader
119	    records: tuple[VcfRecord, ...] = ()
120	    source: str = ""
121	
122	
123	def _line_error(source: str, line_number: int, message: str) -> VcfFormatError:
124	    return VcfFormatError(f"{source}:{line_number}: {message}")
125	
126	
127	def _is_plain_allele(allele: str) -> bool:
128	    """Whether *allele* is an ordinary sequence allele of real bases.
129	
130	    The gVCF spanning value ``*``, the missing value ``.``, symbolic
131	    alleles (``<DEL>``) and break-end alleles (``]chr:123]N``, ``N.``)
132	    are not plain.
133	    """
134	    if not allele or allele == "*" or allele == ".":
135	        return False
136	    if "<" in allele or ">" in allele:
137	        return False
138	    if "[" in allele or "]" in allele or "." in allele or "*" in allele:
139	        return False
140	    return True
141	
142	
143	def _validate_allele(allele: str) -> str:
144	    """Upper-case and validate one ordinary sequence allele."""
145	    upper = allele.upper()
146	    for offset, symbol in enumerate(upper):
147	        if symbol not in _VALID_BASES:
148	            raise ValueError(
149	                f"invalid allele symbol {symbol!r} at offset {offset} of {allele!r}"
150	            )
151	    return upper
152	
153	
154	def _parse_pos(pos_text: str, source: str, number: int) -> int:
155	    if not pos_text or any(char < "0" or char > "9" for char in pos_text):
156	        raise _line_error(
157	            source, number, f"POS {pos_text!r} is not a positive integer"
158	        )
159	    pos = int(pos_text)
160	    if pos <= 0:
161	        raise _line_error(
162	            source, number, f"POS {pos_text!r} is not a positive integer"
163	        )
164	    return pos
165	
166	
167	def _parse_record_line(
168	    line: str, number: int, source: str, samples: Sequence[str]
169	) -> VcfRecord:
170	    fields = line.split("\t")
171	    if len(fields) < _MIN_COLUMNS:
172	        raise _line_error(
173	            source,
174	            number,
175	            f"expected at least 8 tab-separated columns, got {len(fields)}",
176	        )
177	    if samples:
178	        expected = _MIN_COLUMNS + 1 + len(samples)
179	        if len(fields) != expected:
180	            raise _line_error(
181	                source,
182	                number,
183	                f"expected {expected} columns to match the #CHROM header, got {len(fields)}",
184	            )
185	        format_text = fields[8]
186	        if not format_text:
187	            raise _line_error(source, number, "empty FORMAT column")
188	        sample_text = tuple(fields[9:])
189	    else:
190	        if len(fields) != _MIN_COLUMNS:
191	            raise _line_error(
192	                source,
193	                number,
194	                f"expected 8 columns to match the sample-less #CHROM header, "
195	                f"got {len(fields)}",
196	            )
197	        format_text = None
198	        sample_text = ()
199	
200	    chrom, pos_text, ident, ref_text, alt_text, qual, flt, info = fields[:8]
201	
202	    if not chrom:
203	        raise _line_error(source, number, "empty CHROM column")
204	    pos = _parse_pos(pos_text, source, number)
205	
206	    if not ref_text:
207	        raise _line_error(source, number, "empty REF allele")
208	    try:
209	        ref = _validate_allele(ref_text)
210	    except ValueError as exc:
211	        raise _line_error(source, number, str(exc)) from None
212	
213	    if not alt_text:
214	        raise _line_error(source, number, "empty ALT column")
215	    alts: list[str] = []
216	    for allele in alt_text.split(","):
217	        if allele == "":
218	            raise _line_error(source, number, "empty ALT allele")
219	        if not _is_plain_allele(allele):
220	            alts.append(allele)
221	            continue
222	        try:
223	            alts.append(_validate_allele(allele))
224	        except ValueError as exc:
225	            raise _line_error(source, number, str(exc)) from None
226	
227	    return VcfRecord(
228	        chrom=chrom,
229	        pos=pos,
230	        id=ident,
231	        ref=ref,
232	        alt=tuple(alts),
233	        qual=qual,
234	        filter=flt,
235	        info=info,
236	        format_text=format_text,
237	        sample_text=sample_text,
238	        line_number=number,
239	    )
240	
241	
242	def _parse_header_line(
243	    line: str, number: int, source: str
244	) -> tuple[str, ...]:
245	    """Validate the ``#CHROM`` line and return its sample names."""
246	    columns = line.split("\t")
247	    if tuple(columns[:8]) != _FIXED_COLUMNS:
248	        raise _line_error(
249	            source,
250	            number,
251	            "the first eight #CHROM header columns must be exactly "
252	            "#CHROM\\tPOS\\tID\\tREF\\tALT\\tQUAL\\tFILTER\\tINFO",
253	        )
254	    tail = columns[8:]
255	    if not tail:
256	        return ()
257	    if tail[0] != "FORMAT":
258	        raise _line_error(
259	            source, number, "the ninth column, when present, must be FORMAT"
260	        )
261	    samples = tuple(tail[1:])
262	    if not samples:
263	        raise _line_error(source, number, "FORMAT column requires at least one sample")
264	    if any(not sample for sample in samples):
265	        raise _line_error(source, number, "empty sample name in #CHROM header")
266	    return samples
267	
268	
269	def read_vcf(
270	    source: "str | os.PathLike[str] | io.TextIOBase",
271	) -> VcfFile:
272	    """Read and validate a whole VCF document from *source*.
273	
274	    *source* is either a filesystem path (``str`` or :class:`os.PathLike`)
275	    or an already-open text stream.  ``##`` meta-information lines are
276	    kept verbatim and in order; exactly one legal ``#CHROM`` line is
277	    required and every data row must match its columns.  Records are
278	    returned in input order.
279	
280	    Raises :class:`VcfFormatError` for malformed input and :class:`OSError`
281	    when opening a path fails.
282	    """
283	    if isinstance(source, io.IOBase):
284	        stream: io.TextIOBase = source
285	        source_name = getattr(stream, "name", None)
286	        if not isinstance(source_name, str) or not source_name:
287	            source_name = "<stream>"
288	        close = False
289	    elif isinstance(source, (str, os.PathLike)):
290	        path = os.fspath(source)
291	        stream = open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", newline="")
292	        source_name = path
293	        close = True
294	    else:
295	        raise TypeError("source must be a text path or a text stream")
296	
297	    try:
298	        meta_lines: list[str] = []
299	        samples: tuple[str, ...] | None = None
300	        records: list[VcfRecord] = []
301	
302	        for number, raw_line in enumerate(stream, start=1):
303	            line = raw_line.rstrip("\r\n")
304	            if line.startswith("##"):
305	                if samples is not None:
306	                    raise _line_error(
307	                        source_name,
308	                        number,
309	                        "meta-information line after the #CHROM header",
310	                    )
311	                meta_lines.append(line)
312	            elif line.startswith("#"):
313	                if samples is not None:
314	                    raise _line_error(
315	                        source_name, number, "duplicate #CHROM column header"
316	                    )
317	                samples = _parse_header_line(line, number, source_name)
318	            else:
319	                if samples is None:
320	                    raise _line_error(
321	                        source_name, number, "data row before the #CHROM column header"
322	                    )
323	                records.append(
324	                    _parse_record_line(line, number, source_name, samples)
325	                )
326	
327	        if samples is None:
328	            raise VcfFormatError(
329	                f"{source_name}:1: missing #CHROM column header"
330	            )
331	        return VcfFile(
332	            VcfHeader(tuple(meta_lines), samples), tuple(records), source_name
333	        )
334	    finally:
335	        if close:
336	            stream.close()
337	
338	
339	def _build_reference(
340	    reference: Iterable[SequenceRecord],
341	) -> tuple[dict[str, str], set[str]]:
342	    """Map CHROM to sequence, tracking identifiers appearing more than once."""
343	    sequences: dict[str, str] = {}
344	    duplicates: set[str] = set()
345	    for record in reference:
346	        if record.identifier in sequences:
347	            duplicates.add(record.identifier)
348	        else:
349	            sequences[record.identifier] = record.sequence
350	    return sequences, duplicates
351	
352	
353	def _record_error(source: str, record: VcfRecord, message: str) -> VcfFormatError:
354	    if source and record.line_number:
355	        return VcfFormatError(f"{source}:{record.line_number}: {message}")
356	    if record.line_number:
357	        return VcfFormatError(f"line {record.line_number}: {message}")
358	    return VcfFormatError(message)
359	
360	
361	def _resolve_chromosome(
362	    record: VcfRecord,
363	    sequences: Mapping[str, str],
364	    duplicates: set[str],
365	) -> str:
366	    if record.chrom in duplicates:
367	        raise ReferenceMismatchError(
368	            f"CHROM {record.chrom} POS {record.pos}: CHROM occurs more than once "
369	            "in the reference"
370	        )
371	    try:
372	        return sequences[record.chrom]
373	    except KeyError:
374	        raise ReferenceMismatchError(
375	            f"CHROM {record.chrom} POS {record.pos}: no matching record in the reference"
376	        ) from None
377	
378	
379	def _minimize(
380	    pos: int, ref: str, alts: Sequence[str]
381	) -> tuple[int, str, tuple[str, ...]]:
382	    """Remove the common suffix and prefix shared by all alleles.
383	
384	    At least one base is always retained per allele and *pos* (1-based)
385	    is advanced by the number of stripped leading bases.
386	    """
387	    # Common suffix: compare each ALT against REF up to the shorter
388	    # length, always leaving at least one base per allele.
389	    suffix = 0
390	    while True:
391	        index = len(ref) - 1 - suffix
392	        if index <= 0:
393	            break
394	        ref_base = ref[index]
395	        ok = True
396	        for alt in alts:
397	            alt_index = len(alt) - 1 - suffix
398	            if alt_index <= 0 or alt[alt_index] != ref_base:
399	                ok = False
400	                break
401	        if not ok:
402	            break
403	        suffix += 1
404	    if suffix:
405	        ref = ref[: len(ref) - suffix]
406	        alts = tuple(alt[: len(alt) - suffix] for alt in alts)
407	
408	    # Common prefix: at least one base must remain in every allele.
409	    prefix = 0
410	    shortest = min(len(ref), min(len(alt) for alt in alts))
411	    while prefix < shortest - 1 and all(
412	        alt[prefix] == ref[prefix] for alt in alts
413	    ):
414	        prefix += 1
415	    if prefix:
416	        ref = ref[prefix:]
417	        alts = tuple(alt[prefix:] for alt in alts)
418	        pos += prefix
419	
420	    return pos, ref, tuple(alts)
421	
422	
423	def _lengths_differ(ref: str, alts: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
424	    return any(len(alt) != len(ref) for alt in alts)
425	
426	
427	def _normalize_against(
428	    record: VcfRecord,
429	    sequences: Mapping[str, str],
430	    duplicates: set[str],
431	    source: str,
432	) -> VcfRecord:
433	    chromosome = _resolve_chromosome(record, sequences, duplicates)
434	
435	    end = record.pos - 1 + len(record.ref)
436	    if record.pos < 1 or end > len(chromosome):
437	        raise _record_error(
438	            source,
439	            record,
440	            f"CHROM {record.chrom} POS {record.pos}: REF of length {len(record.ref)} "
441	            f"is out of bounds for a reference of length {len(chromosome)}",
442	        )
443	
444	    expected = chromosome[record.pos - 1 : end].upper()
445	    if expected != record.ref:
446	        raise ReferenceMismatchError(
447	            f"CHROM {record.chrom} POS {record.pos}: REF does not match the "
448	            f"reference: expected {expected!r}, found {record.ref!r}"
449	        )
450	
451	    if not all(_is_plain_allele(allele) for allele in record.alt):
452	        # Symbolic, break-end, spanning or missing ALT: verify only.
453	        return record
454	
455	    pos, ref, alts = _minimize(record.pos, record.ref, record.alt)
456	
457	    # Left-align: prepend the preceding reference base to every allele
458	    # and re-minimize.  A move only happens when re-minimization removes
459	    # a (different) right-hand base, i.e. the extended window represents
460	    # the same haplotypes; once a step leaves the alleles unchanged the
461	    # minimum POS has been reached.
462	    while pos > 1 and _lengths_differ(ref, alts):
463	        preceding = chromosome[pos - 2].upper()
464	        next_pos, next_ref, next_alts = _minimize(
465	            pos - 1,
466	            preceding + ref,
467	            tuple(preceding + alt for alt in alts),
468	        )
469	        if (next_pos, next_ref, next_alts) == (pos, ref, alts):
470	            break
471	        pos, ref, alts = next_pos, next_ref, next_alts
472	
473	    return replace(record, pos=pos, ref=ref, alt=alts)
474	
475	
476	def normalize_record(
477	    record: VcfRecord,
478	    reference: "Mapping[str, str] | Iterable[SequenceRecord]",
479	) -> VcfRecord:
480	    """Normalize one record against *reference*.
481	
482	    *reference* is either a mapping of CHROM to upper-case reference
483	    sequence or an iterable of :class:`~genome_variant.sequence_io.SequenceRecord`
484	    (duplicate identifiers raise :class:`ReferenceMismatchError`).
485	
486	    The REF fragment at POS is always verified.  Records whose ALT
487	    contains a symbolic, break-end, spanning (``*``) or missing (``.``)
488	    allele are returned unchanged.  Otherwise all sequence alleles are
489	    trimmed of their shared suffix and prefix (one base is always kept)
490	    and, when allele lengths differ, left-shifted across repeated
491	    reference bases to the smallest POS representing the same
492	    haplotypes, re-minimizing after every shift.  ID, QUAL, FILTER,
493	    INFO, FORMAT, sample text and ALT order are preserved.
494	
495	    Raises :class:`ReferenceMismatchError` for an absent/duplicate CHROM
496	    or a REF that disagrees with the reference, and
497	    :class:`VcfFormatError` for a record that runs past the reference.
498	    """
499	    if isinstance(reference, Mapping):
500	        sequences = dict(reference)
501	        duplicates: set[str] = set()
502	    else:
503	        sequences, duplicates = _build_reference(reference)
504	    return _normalize_against(record, sequences, duplicates, "")
505	
506	
507	def normalize_vcf(
508	    document: VcfFile,
509	    reference: "Mapping[str, str] | Iterable[SequenceRecord]",
510	) -> VcfFile:
511	    """Normalize every record of *document* against *reference*.
512	
513	    Record order is preserved; see :func:`normalize_record` for the
514	    per-record rules.  Every record is validated before the normalized
515	    document is returned, so an error never comes with partial output.
516	    """
517	    if isinstance(reference, Mapping):
518	        sequences = dict(reference)
519	        duplicates: set[str] = set()
520	    else:
521	        sequences, duplicates = _build_reference(reference)
522	
523	    normalized = tuple(
524	        _normalize_against(record, sequences, duplicates, document.source)
525	        for record in document.records
526	    )
527	    return VcfFile(document.header, normalized, document.source)
528	
529	
530	def _record_line(record: VcfRecord) -> str:
531	    fields = [
532	        record.chrom,
533	        str(record.pos),
534	        record.id,
535	        record.ref,
536	        record.alt_text,
537	        record.qual,
538	        record.filter,
539	        record.info,
540	    ]
541	    if record.format_text is not None:
542	        fields.append(record.format_text)
543	        fields.extend(record.sample_text)
544	    return "\t".join(fields)
545	
546	
547	def render_vcf(document: VcfFile) -> str:
548	    """Serialize *document* to VCF text.
549	
550	    Output uses tabs and ``"\\n"`` line endings and always ends with
551	    exactly one trailing newline; a record-less VCF still writes the
552	    complete header (``##`` lines followed by the ``#CHROM`` line).
553	    """
554	    lines = list(document.header.meta_lines)
555	    lines.append("\t".join(document.header.column_names))
556	    lines.extend(_record_line(record) for record in document.records)
557	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
558	
559	
560	def write_vcf(
561	    document: VcfFile,
562	    output: "str | os.PathLike[str] | io.TextIOBase",
563	) -> None:
564	    """Write *document* to *output* as VCF text.
565	
566	    Tabs and ``"\\n"`` are used throughout with exactly one trailing
567	    newline; an empty-record VCF still writes the complete header.
568	    """
569	    text = render_vcf(document)
570	    if isinstance(output, io.IOBase):
571	        output.write(text)
572	    elif isinstance(output, (str, os.PathLike)):
573	        with open(os.fspath(output), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
574	            stream.write(text)
575	    else:
576	        raise TypeError("output must be a text path or a text stream")
577

1	"""FASTA/FASTQ reading and normalization.
2	
3	Public API:
4	
5	- :class:`SequenceRecord` — one sequence with identifier, description and
6	  optional per-base quality values.
7	- :func:`read_sequences` — lazily read records from a text path or text
8	  stream; the format is ``"fasta"``, ``"fastq"`` or ``"auto"``.
9	- :func:`write_sequences` — write records in FASTA or FASTQ form.
10	
11	Sequences only contain the IUPAC DNA symbols ``ACGTRYSWKMBDHVN``.  FASTQ
12	quality values use the Phred+33 encoding with ASCII characters 33–126.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import io
18	import os
19	from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
20	from dataclasses import dataclass
21	
22	__all__ = [
23	    "SequenceRecord",
24	    "SequenceFormatError",
25	    "SequenceValidationError",
26	    "read_sequences",
27	    "write_sequences",
28	]
29	
30	_VALID_BASES = frozenset("ACGTRYSWKMBDHVN")
31	_INPUT_FORMATS = ("fasta", "fastq", "auto")
32	_OUTPUT_FORMATS = ("fasta", "fastq")
33	
34	
35	class SequenceFormatError(ValueError):
36	    """Malformed FASTA/FASTQ input (structure, identifiers, lengths)."""
37	
38	
39	class SequenceValidationError(ValueError):
40	    """A sequence contains a symbol outside the allowed IUPAC set."""
41	
42	
43	@dataclass(frozen=True)
44	class SequenceRecord:
45	    """A single sequence record.
46	
47	    ``identifier`` is the first whitespace-delimited field of the title
48	    line; ``description`` holds the remainder (``""`` when absent).
49	    ``quality`` is ``None`` for FASTA records and a tuple of Phred scores
50	    for FASTQ records.
51	    """
52	
53	    identifier: str
54	    sequence: str
55	    description: str = ""
56	    quality: tuple[int, ...] | None = None
57	
58	
59	def _clean_sequence(raw: str) -> str:
60	    """Strip in-line whitespace and upper-case a raw sequence fragment."""
61	    return "".join(raw.split()).upper()
62	
63	
64	def _validate_sequence(identifier: str, sequence: str) -> None:
65	    for position, symbol in enumerate(sequence, start=1):
66	        if symbol not in _VALID_BASES:
67	            raise SequenceValidationError(
68	                f"record {identifier!r}: invalid symbol {symbol!r} at position {position}"
69	            )
70	
71	
72	def _split_title(title: str, source: str, line_number: int) -> tuple[str, str]:
73	    fields = title.split(None, 1)
74	    if not fields:
75	        raise SequenceFormatError(f"{source}:{line_number}: empty sequence identifier")
76	    identifier = fields[0]
77	    description = fields[1] if len(fields) == 2 else ""
78	    return identifier, description
79	
80	
81	def _line_error(source: str, line_number: int, message: str) -> SequenceFormatError:
82	    return SequenceFormatError(f"{source}:{line_number}: {message}")
83	
84	
85	def _fasta_records(
86	    lines: Iterator[tuple[int, str]], source: str
87	) -> Iterator[SequenceRecord]:
88	    header_line: str | None = None
89	    header_number = 0
90	    seq_parts: list[str] = []
91	
92	    for number, raw_line in lines:
93	        line = raw_line.rstrip("\r\n")
94	        if line.startswith(">"):
95	            if header_line is not None:
96	                yield _finish_fasta(header_line, header_number, seq_parts, source)
97	            header_line = line
98	            header_number = number
99	            seq_parts = []
100	        elif line.strip():
101	            if header_line is None:
102	                raise _line_error(
103	                    source,
104	                    number,
105	                    "content before first title line (expected a line starting with '>')",
106	                )
107	            seq_parts.append(line)
108	        # Blank lines outside or inside a record are ignored.
109	
110	    if header_line is not None:
111	        yield _finish_fasta(header_line, header_number, seq_parts, source)
112	
113	
114	def _finish_fasta(
115	    header_line: str, header_number: int, parts: list[str], source: str
116	) -> SequenceRecord:
117	    identifier, description = _split_title(header_line[1:], source, header_number)
118	    sequence = _clean_sequence("".join(parts))
119	    if not sequence:
120	        raise _line_error(source, header_number, "empty sequence")
121	    _validate_sequence(identifier, sequence)
122	    return SequenceRecord(identifier, sequence, description)
123	
124	
125	def _check_quality_segment(segment: str, source: str, line_number: int) -> None:
126	    for char in segment:
127	        value = ord(char)
128	        if value < 33 or value > 126:
129	            raise _line_error(
130	                source,
131	                line_number,
132	                f"quality character {char!r} is outside the ASCII 33-126 range",
133	            )
134	
135	
136	def _fastq_records(
137	    lines: Iterator[tuple[int, str]], source: str
138	) -> Iterator[SequenceRecord]:
139	    # State machine over logical lines.  Sequence and quality may each
140	    # span several physical lines; record boundaries are determined by the
141	    # '+' separator and the number of quality characters matching the
142	    # sequence length.
143	    header_line: str | None = None
144	    header_number = 0
145	    seq_parts: list[str] = []
146	    qual_segments: list[str] = []
147	    in_quality = False
148	
149	    for number, raw_line in lines:
150	        line = raw_line.rstrip("\r\n")
151	
152	        if header_line is None:
153	            if not line:
154	                raise _line_error(
155	                    source,
156	                    number,
157	                    "incomplete FASTQ record (expected a title line starting with '@')",
158	                )
159	            if not line.startswith("@"):
160	                raise _line_error(
161	                    source, number, "expected a FASTQ title line starting with '@'"
162	                )
163	            header_line = line
164	            header_number = number
165	            seq_parts = []
166	            qual_segments = []
167	            in_quality = False
168	            continue
169	
170	        if not in_quality:
171	            if line.startswith("+"):
172	                plus_title = line[1:]
173	                if plus_title and plus_title != header_line[1:]:
174	                    raise _line_error(
175	                        source,
176	                        number,
177	                        "FASTQ separator title does not match the record title",
178	                    )
179	                if not _clean_sequence("".join(seq_parts)):
180	                    raise _line_error(source, header_number, "empty sequence")
181	                in_quality = True
182	            else:
183	                if not line.strip():
184	                    raise _line_error(source, number, "empty sequence")
185	                seq_parts.append(line)
186	            continue
187	
188	        if not line:
189	            raise _line_error(source, number, "incomplete FASTQ record (missing quality values)")
190	        _check_quality_segment(line, source, number)
191	        qual_segments.append(line)
192	
193	        sequence = _clean_sequence("".join(seq_parts))
194	        quality_text = "".join(qual_segments)
195	        if len(quality_text) > len(sequence):
196	            raise _line_error(
197	                source,
198	                number,
199	                f"quality length {len(quality_text)} does not match sequence length {len(sequence)}",
200	            )
201	        if len(quality_text) == len(sequence):
202	            yield _finish_fastq(
203	                header_line, header_number, sequence, quality_text, source
204	            )
205	            header_line = None
206	
207	    if header_line is not None:
208	        raise _line_error(source, header_number, "incomplete FASTQ record")
209	
210	
211	def _finish_fastq(
212	    header_line: str,
213	    header_number: int,
214	    sequence: str,
215	    quality_text: str,
216	    source: str,
217	) -> SequenceRecord:
218	    identifier, description = _split_title(header_line[1:], source, header_number)
219	    if not sequence:
220	        raise _line_error(source, header_number, "empty sequence")
221	    _validate_sequence(identifier, sequence)
222	    if len(quality_text) != len(sequence):
223	        raise _line_error(
224	            source,
225	            header_number,
226	            f"quality length {len(quality_text)} does not match sequence length {len(sequence)}",
227	        )
228	    quality = tuple(ord(char) - 33 for char in quality_text)
229	    return SequenceRecord(identifier, sequence, description, quality)
230	
231	
232	def _enumerate_lines(stream: Iterable[str]) -> Iterator[tuple[int, str]]:
233	    for number, line in enumerate(stream, start=1):
234	        yield number, line
235	
236	
237	def read_sequences(
238	    source: "str | os.PathLike[str] | io.TextIOBase",
239	    format: str = "auto",
240	) -> Iterator[SequenceRecord]:
241	    """Lazily read sequence records from *source*.
242	
243	    *source* is either a filesystem path (``str`` or :class:`os.PathLike`)
244	    or an already-open text stream.  *format* is ``"fasta"``, ``"fastq"``
245	    or ``"auto"``; with ``"auto"`` the format is detected from the first
246	    non-empty line (``>`` → FASTA, ``@`` → FASTQ).
247	
248	    Records are produced in input order.  Errors raised while opening a
249	    path propagate as :class:`OSError`; malformed input raises
250	    :class:`SequenceFormatError` or :class:`SequenceValidationError`
251	    during iteration and are never swallowed.
252	    """
253	    if format not in _INPUT_FORMATS:
254	        raise ValueError(
255	            f"unsupported format {format!r}; expected one of {', '.join(_INPUT_FORMATS)}"
256	        )
257	
258	    if isinstance(source, io.IOBase):
259	        stream: io.TextIOBase = source
260	        source_name = getattr(stream, "name", None)
261	        if not isinstance(source_name, str) or not source_name:
262	            source_name = "<stream>"
263	        close = False
264	    elif isinstance(source, (str, os.PathLike)):
265	        path = os.fspath(source)
266	        stream = open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", newline="")
267	        source_name = path
268	        close = True
269	    else:
270	        raise TypeError("source must be a text path or a text stream")
271	
272	    try:
273	        yield from _read_from_stream(stream, source_name, format)
274	    finally:
275	        if close:
276	            stream.close()
277	
278	
279	def _read_from_stream(
280	    stream: Iterable[str], source_name: str, format: str
281	) -> Iterator[SequenceRecord]:
282	    numbered = _enumerate_lines(stream)
283	
284	    first_number = 0
285	    first_line: str | None = None
286	    for number, raw_line in numbered:
287	        candidate = raw_line.rstrip("\r\n")
288	        if candidate.strip():
289	            first_number = number
290	            first_line = candidate
291	            break
292	
293	    if first_line is None:
294	        if format == "auto":
295	            raise SequenceFormatError(
296	                f"{source_name}: empty input; cannot determine format"
297	            )
298	        raise SequenceFormatError(f"{source_name}: empty input")
299	
300	    if format == "auto":
301	        if first_line.startswith(">"):
302	            detected = "fasta"
303	        elif first_line.startswith("@"):
304	            detected = "fastq"
305	        else:
306	            raise _line_error(
307	                source_name,
308	                first_number,
309	                "cannot determine format: first non-empty line must start with '>' or '@'",
310	            )
311	    else:
312	        detected = format
313	
314	    def replay() -> Iterator[tuple[int, str]]:
315	        yield first_number, first_line + "\n"
316	        yield from numbered
317	
318	    # The per-format parsers reject a first line that lacks their title
319	    # marker themselves (reported as content before / unexpected title).
320	    if detected == "fasta":
321	        yield from _fasta_records(replay(), source_name)
322	    else:
323	        yield from _fastq_records(replay(), source_name)
324	
325	
326	def write_sequences(
327	    records: Iterable[SequenceRecord],
328	    output: "str | os.PathLike[str] | io.TextIOBase",
329	    format: str = "fasta",
330	    line_width: int = 60,
331	) -> None:
332	    """Write *records* to *output* in FASTA or FASTQ form.
333	
334	    FASTA sequences are wrapped at *line_width* characters (a positive
335	    integer); FASTQ always uses the fixed four-line layout regardless of
336	    *line_width*.  Records without quality values cannot be written as
337	    FASTQ.  Output uses ``"\\n"`` line endings and ends with exactly one
338	    trailing newline.
339	    """
340	    if format not in _OUTPUT_FORMATS:
341	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported format {format!r}; expected 'fasta' or 'fastq'")
342	    if not isinstance(line_width, int) or isinstance(line_width, bool) or line_width <= 0:
343	        raise ValueError("line_width must be a positive integer")
344	
345	    if isinstance(output, io.IOBase):
346	        stream: io.TextIOBase = output
347	        close = False
348	    elif isinstance(output, (str, os.PathLike)):
349	        stream = open(os.fspath(output), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="")
350	        close = True
351	    else:
352	        raise TypeError("output must be a text path or a text stream")
353	
354	    try:
355	        for record in records:
356	            _validate_sequence(record.identifier, record.sequence)
357	            if format == "fasta":
358	                stream.write(_format_fasta_record(record, line_width))
359	            else:
360	                stream.write(_format_fastq_record(record))
361	    finally:
362	        if close:
363	            stream.close()
364	
365	
366	def _format_title(record: SequenceRecord) -> str:
367	    if record.description:
368	        return record.identifier + " " + record.description
369	    return record.identifier
370	
371	
372	def _format_fasta_record(record: SequenceRecord, line_width: int) -> str:
373	    parts = [">" + _format_title(record) + "\n"]
374	    sequence = record.sequence
375	    for start in range(0, len(sequence), line_width):
376	        parts.append(sequence[start : start + line_width])
377	        parts.append("\n")
378	    return "".join(parts)
379	
380	
381	def _format_fastq_record(record: SequenceRecord) -> str:
382	    if record.quality is None:
383	        raise ValueError(
384	            f"record {record.identifier!r} has no quality values; cannot write it as FASTQ"
385	        )
386	    if len(record.quality) != len(record.sequence):
387	        raise ValueError(
388	            f"record {record.identifier!r}: quality length does not match sequence length"
389	        )
390	    quality_chars = []
391	    for value in record.quality:
392	        if not 0 <= value <= 93:
393	            raise ValueError(
394	                f"record {record.identifier!r}: quality score {value} is outside the "
395	                "Phred+33 range 0-93"
396	            )
397	        quality_chars.append(chr(value + 33))
398	    title = _format_title(record)
399	    return f"@{title}\n{record.sequence}\n+{title}\n{''.join(quality_chars)}\n"

1	"""Cross-entry consistency regression tests.
2	
3	These tests pin the public composition contract: for one shared
4	multi-record reference, one ordered set of FASTQ samples and one set of
5	calling thresholds, running ``batch-call-variants`` is byte-for-byte
6	equivalent to running ``call-variants`` once per sample (in manifest
7	order) and feeding the resulting single-sample VCFs to
8	``summarize-variants``.
9	
10	No production behavior is exercised beyond what the three entry points
11	already promise; the same contract is checked for the default SNV-only
12	mode and for ``--call-indels``, from different working directories, for
13	empty inputs, for a failing later sample, for repeated runs and for
14	different physical chunking of the input reads.  Invalid thresholds,
15	duplicate sample names, bad references and file-access failures keep
16	their existing exit codes and exception types on both paths; the
17	contract is never achieved by relaxing validation.
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import json
23	import sys
24	from io import StringIO
25	from pathlib import Path
26	
27	import pytest
28	
29	from genome_variant.batch import BatchManifestError, batch_call_variants
30	from genome_variant.calling import VariantCallingError, call_variants
31	from genome_variant.summary import ManifestError, summarize_variants
32	from genome_variant.sequence_io import SequenceRecord, write_sequences
33	from genome_variant.cli import main
34	
35	# -- Fixture data -----------------------------------------------------------
36	
37	# Three reference records deliberately ordered so that variants appear
38	# out of reference order across samples; merged output must be sorted by
39	# reference order rather than encounter order.
40	C1 = "ACGTACGTACAA"            # SNV sites at POS 5 (A) and POS 8 (T)
41	C2 = "TAACGTTTCC"             # reverse-strand evidence site at POS 3 (A)
42	C3 = "ACGTACAAAATCGAC"        # A-run; an inserted A left-aligns to POS 6
43	REFERENCE_TEXT = f">c1\n{C1}\n>c2\n{C2}\n>c3\n{C3}\n"
44	REFERENCE_RECORDS = (
45	    SequenceRecord("c1", C1),
46	    SequenceRecord("c2", C2),
47	    SequenceRecord("c3", C3),
48	)
49	
50	HIGH = "I"   # Phred 40, above the default quality floor of 20
51	LOW = "%"    # Phred 4, below the default quality floor of 20
52	
53	SAMPLE_ORDER = ("s1", "s2", "s3", "s4", "s5")
54	
55	
56	def _rc(sequence: str) -> str:
57	    return sequence.translate(str.maketrans("ACGT", "TGCA"))[::-1]
58	
59	
60	def _substitute(sequence: str, index: int, base: str) -> str:
61	    chars = list(sequence)
62	    chars[index] = base
63	    return "".join(chars)
64	
65	
66	def _record(identifier: str, sequence: str, quality: str | None = None):
67	    if quality is None:
68	        quality = HIGH * len(sequence)
69	    return SequenceRecord(
70	        identifier,
71	        sequence,
72	        quality=tuple(ord(char) - 33 for char in quality),
73	    )
74	
75	
76	# c2 POS 3 A>T as a forward read; its reverse complement is how the
77	# reverse-strand evidence appears in the FASTQ.
78	_C2_VARIANT_READ = _substitute(C2, 2, "T")
79	
80	# Insertion of one A into the c3 A-run, sampled at three different raw
81	# breakpoints/offsets; every raw event normalizes to c3:6 C>CA.
82	_INS_FULL = C3[:6] + "A" + C3[6:]
83	_INS_SHORT_B = C3[2:10] + "A" + C3[10:15]
84	_INS_SHORT_C = C3[1:8] + "A" + C3[8:14]
85	
86	
87	def _sample_records() -> dict[str, list[SequenceRecord]]:
88	    """Build the shared sample set (fresh record objects for every call)."""
89	    return {
90	        # s1: heterozygous c1:5 A>T plus heterozygous c2:3 A>T.
91	        # Evidence mixes both strands, a low-quality variant base on each
92	        # strand (excluded from AC and DP at that site), matching wild
93	        # reads and an unmapped all-N read.
94	        "s1": [
95	            _record("s1f1", _substitute(C1, 4, "T")),
96	            _record("s1f2", _substitute(C1, 4, "T")),
97	            _record("s1fw", C1),
98	            _record("s1flq", _substitute(C1, 4, "T"), HIGH * 4 + LOW + HIGH * 7),
99	            _record("s1r1", _rc(_C2_VARIANT_READ)),
100	            _record("s1r2", _rc(_C2_VARIANT_READ)),
101	            # Low quality at the variant column on the reverse strand:
102	            # original-read index 7 maps to aligned index 2.
103	            _record("s1rlq", _rc(_C2_VARIANT_READ), HIGH * 7 + LOW + HIGH * 2),
104	            _record("s1rw1", C2),
105	            _record("s1rw2", _rc(C2)),
106	            _record("s1unmapped", "NNNNNNNN"),
107	        ],
108	        # s2: c1:5 A>T stays heterozygous while c1:8 T>A is homozygous;
109	        # ten reads cover both sites so DP is shared per site.
110	        "s2": [
111	            *[_record(f"s2a{i}", _substitute(C1, 4, "T")) for i in range(2)],
112	            *[_record(f"s2b{i}", _substitute(C1, 7, "A")) for i in range(8)],
113	        ],
114	        # s3: no variant anywhere (wild reads, one low-quality leading
115	        # base and an unmapped read).
116	        "s3": [
117	            _record("s3w1", C1),
118	            _record("s3lq", C2, LOW + HIGH * 9),
119	            _record("s3unmapped", "NNNNNNNN"),
120	            _record("s3w2", C1),
121	        ],
122	        # s4: heterozygous left-aligned insertion c3:6 C>CA; evidence
123	        # arrives from different raw breakpoints and both strands.
124	        "s4": [
125	            _record("s4a", _INS_FULL),
126	            _record("s4b", _rc(_INS_SHORT_B)),
127	            _record("s4c", _rc(_INS_SHORT_C)),
128	            _record("s4w", C3),
129	        ],
130	        # s5: the same left-aligned insertion, homozygous.
131	        "s5": [
132	            _record("s5a", _INS_FULL),
133	            _record("s5b", _INS_SHORT_B),
134	            _record("s5c", _INS_SHORT_C),
135	        ],
136	    }
137	
138	
139	# Expected per-variant summaries under the default thresholds.
140	EXPECTED_DEFAULT_SNV = [
141	    {
142	        "chrom": "c1",
143	        "pos": 5,
144	        "ref": "A",
145	        "alt": "T",
146	        "sample_count": 2,
147	        "allele_count": 2,

197	def run_cli(argv, stdin: str = ""):
198	    old_in, old_out, old_err = sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr
199	    sys.stdin = StringIO(stdin)
200	    sys.stdout = StringIO()
201	    sys.stderr = StringIO()
202	    try:
203	        try:
204	            code = main(argv)
205	        except SystemExit as exc:
206	            code = exc.code
207	    finally:
208	        out, err = sys.stdout.getvalue(), sys.stderr.getvalue()
209	        sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr = old_in, old_out, old_err
210	    return code, out, err

552	def _wrapped_fastq_text(records, chunk: int) -> str:
553	    """Serialize records with sequence/quality wrapped every *chunk* bases.
554	
555	    The FASTQ reader accumulates wrapped sequence and quality segments
556	    into the same logical records, so this varies the physical line
557	    chunking seen during iteration without changing a single record.
558	    """
559	    lines: list[str] = []
560	    for record in records:
561	        quality = "".join(chr(score + 33) for score in record.quality)
562	        lines.append("@" + record.identifier)
563	        for start in range(0, len(record.sequence), chunk):
564	            lines.append(record.sequence[start : start + chunk])
565	        lines.append("+" + record.identifier)
566	        for start in range(0, len(quality), chunk):
567	            lines.append(quality[start : start + chunk])
568	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

"""Cross-entry consistency regression tests.

These tests pin the public composition contract: for one shared
multi-record reference, one ordered set of FASTQ samples and one set of
calling thresholds, running ``batch-call-variants`` is byte-for-byte
equivalent to running ``call-variants`` once per sample (in manifest
order) and feeding the resulting single-sample VCFs to
``summarize-variants``.

No production behavior is exercised beyond what the three entry points
already promise; the same contract is checked for the default SNV-only
mode and for ``--call-indels``, from different working directories, for
empty inputs, for a failing later sample, for repeated runs and for
different physical chunking of the input reads.  Invalid thresholds,
duplicate sample names, bad references and file-access failures keep
their existing exit codes and exception types on both paths; the
contract is never achieved by relaxing validation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from genome_variant.batch import BatchManifestError, batch_call_variants
from genome_variant.calling import VariantCallingError, call_variants
from genome_variant.summary import ManifestError, summarize_variants
from genome_variant.sequence_io import SequenceRecord, write_sequences
from genome_variant.cli import main

# -- Fixture data -----------------------------------------------------------

# Three reference records deliberately ordered so that variants appear
# out of reference order across samples; merged output must be sorted by
# reference order rather than encounter order.
C1 = "ACGTACGTACAA"            # SNV sites at POS 5 (A) and POS 8 (T)
C2 = "TAACGTTTCC"             # reverse-strand evidence site at POS 3 (A)
C3 = "ACGTACAAAATCGAC"        # A-run; an inserted A left-aligns to POS 6
REFERENCE_TEXT = f">c1\n{C1}\n>c2\n{C2}\n>c3\n{C3}\n"
REFERENCE_RECORDS = (
    SequenceRecord("c1", C1),
    SequenceRecord("c2", C2),
    SequenceRecord("c3", C3),
)

HIGH = "I"   # Phred 40, above the default quality floor of 20
LOW = "%"    # Phred 4, below the default quality floor of 20

SAMPLE_ORDER = ("s1", "s2", "s3", "s4", "s5")


def _rc(sequence: str) -> str:
    return sequence.translate(str.maketrans("ACGT", "TGCA"))[::-1]


def _substitute(sequence: str, index: int, base: str) -> str:
    chars = list(sequence)
    chars[index] = base
    return "".join(chars)


def _record(identifier: str, sequence: str, quality: str | None = None):
    if quality is None:
        quality = HIGH * len(sequence)
    return SequenceRecord(
        identifier,
        sequence,
        quality=tuple(ord(char) - 33 for char in quality),
    )


# c2 POS 3 A>T as a forward read; its reverse complement is how the
# reverse-strand evidence appears in the FASTQ.
_C2_VARIANT_READ = _substitute(C2, 2, "T")

# Insertion of one A into the c3 A-run, sampled at three different raw
# breakpoints/offsets; every raw event normalizes to c3:6 C>CA.
_INS_FULL = C3[:6] + "A" + C3[6:]
_INS_SHORT_B = C3[2:10] + "A" + C3[10:15]
_INS_SHORT_C = C3[1:8] + "A" + C3[8:14]


def _sample_records() -> dict[str, list[SequenceRecord]]:
    """Build the shared sample set (fresh record objects for every call)."""
    return {
        # s1: heterozygous c1:5 A>T plus heterozygous c2:3 A>T.
        # Evidence mixes both strands, a low-quality variant base on each
        # strand (excluded from AC and DP at that site), matching wild
        # reads and an unmapped all-N read.
        "s1": [
            _record("s1f1", _substitute(C1, 4, "T")),
            _record("s1f2", _substitute(C1, 4, "T")),
            _record("s1fw", C1),
            _record("s1flq", _substitute(C1, 4, "T"), HIGH * 4 + LOW + HIGH * 7),
            _record("s1r1", _rc(_C2_VARIANT_READ)),
            _record("s1r2", _rc(_C2_VARIANT_READ)),
            # Low quality at the variant column on the reverse strand:
            # original-read index 7 maps to aligned index 2.
            _record("s1rlq", _rc(_C2_VARIANT_READ), HIGH * 7 + LOW + HIGH * 2),
            _record("s1rw1", C2),
            _record("s1rw2", _rc(C2)),
            _record("s1unmapped", "NNNNNNNN"),
        ],
        # s2: c1:5 A>T stays heterozygous while c1:8 T>A is homozygous;
        # ten reads cover both sites so DP is shared per site.
        "s2": [
            *[_record(f"s2a{i}", _substitute(C1, 4, "T")) for i in range(2)],
            *[_record(f"s2b{i}", _substitute(C1, 7, "A")) for i in range(8)],
        ],
        # s3: no variant anywhere (wild reads, one low-quality leading
        # base and an unmapped read).
        "s3": [
            _record("s3w1", C1),
            _record("s3lq", C2, LOW + HIGH * 9),
            _record("s3unmapped", "NNNNNNNN"),
            _record("s3w2", C1),
        ],
        # s4: heterozygous left-aligned insertion c3:6 C>CA; evidence
        # arrives from different raw breakpoints and both strands.
        "s4": [
            _record("s4a", _INS_FULL),
            _record("s4b", _rc(_INS_SHORT_B)),
            _record("s4c", _rc(_INS_SHORT_C)),
            _record("s4w", C3),
        ],
        # s5: the same left-aligned insertion, homozygous.
        "s5": [
            _record("s5a", _INS_FULL),
            _record("s5b", _INS_SHORT_B),
            _record("s5c", _INS_SHORT_C),
        ],
    }


# Expected per-variant summaries under the default thresholds.
EXPECTED_DEFAULT_SNV = [
    {
        "chrom": "c1",
        "pos": 5,
        "ref": "A",
        "alt": "T",
        "sample_count": 2,
        "allele_count": 2,
        "depth": 13,
        "samples": [
            {"sample": "s1", "gt": "0/1", "dp": 3, "ad": [1, 2]},
            {"sample": "s2", "gt": "0/1", "dp": 10, "ad": [8, 2]},
        ],
    },
    {
        "chrom": "c1",
        "pos": 8,
        "ref": "T",
        "alt": "A",
        "sample_count": 1,
        "allele_count": 2,
        "depth": 10,
        "samples": [
            {"sample": "s2", "gt": "1/1", "dp": 10, "ad": [2, 8]},
        ],
    },
    {
        "chrom": "c2",
        "pos": 3,
        "ref": "A",
        "alt": "T",
        "sample_count": 1,
        "allele_count": 1,
        "depth": 4,
        "samples": [
            {"sample": "s1", "gt": "0/1", "dp": 4, "ad": [2, 2]},
        ],
    },
]

EXPECTED_DEFAULT_INSERTION = {
    "chrom": "c3",
    "pos": 6,
    "ref": "C",
    "alt": "CA",
    "sample_count": 2,
    "allele_count": 3,
    "depth": 7,
    "samples": [
        {"sample": "s4", "gt": "0/1", "dp": 4, "ad": [1, 3]},
        {"sample": "s5", "gt": "1/1", "dp": 3, "ad": [0, 3]},
    ],
}


# -- CLI harness ------------------------------------------------------------

def run_cli(argv, stdin: str = ""):
    old_in, old_out, old_err = sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr
    sys.stdin = StringIO(stdin)
    sys.stdout = StringIO()
    sys.stderr = StringIO()
    try:
        try:
            code = main(argv)
        except SystemExit as exc:
            code = exc.code
    finally:
        out, err = sys.stdout.getvalue(), sys.stderr.getvalue()
        sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr = old_in, old_out, old_err
    return code, out, err


@pytest.fixture
def workspace(tmp_path):
    """Materialize the reference, per-sample FASTQs and the reads manifest."""
    (tmp_path / "ref.fa").write_text(REFERENCE_TEXT)

    reads_dir = tmp_path / "reads"
    reads_dir.mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "vcfs").mkdir()

    records = _sample_records()
    for sample in SAMPLE_ORDER:
        with open(reads_dir / f"{sample}.fq", "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
            write_sequences(iter(records[sample]), fh, format="fastq")

    manifest = tmp_path / "reads.jsonl"
    manifest.write_text(
        "".join(
            json.dumps({"sample": sample, "reads": f"reads/{sample}.fq"}) + "\n"
            for sample in SAMPLE_ORDER
        )
    )
    return tmp_path


def _batch_argv(workdir: Path, *extra: str) -> list[str]:
    return [
        "batch-call-variants",
        str(workdir / "reads.jsonl"),
        "--reference",
        str(workdir / "ref.fa"),
        *extra,
    ]


def _call_each_sample_then_summarize(workdir: Path, *extra: str):
    """The decomposed path: call-variants per sample, then summarize."""
    for sample in SAMPLE_ORDER:
        code, out, err = run_cli(
            [
                "call-variants",
                str(workdir / "ref.fa"),
                str(workdir / "reads" / f"{sample}.fq"),
                "--sample-name", sample,
                "--output", str(workdir / "vcfs" / f"{sample}.vcf"),
                *extra,
            ]
        )
        assert code == 0, f"call-variants for {sample} failed: {err}"
        assert out == "" and err == ""

    manifest = workdir / "vcfs.jsonl"
    manifest.write_text(
        "".join(
            json.dumps({"sample": sample, "vcf": f"vcfs/{sample}.vcf"}) + "\n"
            for sample in SAMPLE_ORDER
        )
    )
    return run_cli(
        [
            "summarize-variants",
            str(manifest),
            "--reference",
            str(workdir / "ref.fa"),
        ]
    )


def _assert_default_variant_payload(payload, *, indels: bool) -> None:
    expected = list(EXPECTED_DEFAULT_SNV)
    if indels:
        expected.append(EXPECTED_DEFAULT_INSERTION)
    assert payload == expected


# -- The core byte-for-byte contract ----------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "extra,indels",
    [
        ([], False),
        (["--call-indels"], True),
    ],
)
def test_batch_output_byte_identical_to_per_sample_calls_then_summary(
    workspace, extra, indels
) -> None:
    code_batch, out_batch, err_batch = run_cli(_batch_argv(workspace, *extra))
    assert code_batch == 0 and err_batch == ""

    code_sum, out_sum, err_sum = _call_each_sample_then_summarize(workspace, *extra)
    assert code_sum == 0 and err_sum == ""

    # The contract: successful outputs are byte-for-byte identical.
    assert out_batch == out_sum
    assert out_batch.encode("utf-8") == out_sum.encode("utf-8")

    payload = [json.loads(line) for line in out_batch.splitlines()]
    _assert_default_variant_payload(payload, indels=indels)


def test_output_is_structurally_complete_not_just_record_counts(workspace) -> None:
    code, out, err = run_cli(_batch_argv(workspace, "--call-indels"))
    assert code == 0 and err == ""
    payload = [json.loads(line) for line in out.splitlines()]

    # Normalized variant order: reference order (c1, c2, c3), then POS.
    assert [
        tuple(row[key] for key in ("chrom", "pos", "ref", "alt")) for row in payload
    ] == [
        ("c1", 5, "A", "T"),
        ("c1", 8, "T", "A"),
        ("c2", 3, "A", "T"),
        ("c3", 6, "C", "CA"),
    ]

    first = payload[0]
    # Sample order follows the manifest, not per-VCF iteration quirks.
    assert [sample["sample"] for sample in first["samples"]] == ["s1", "s2"]
    # Genotypes, depths and per-allele depths are carried per sample.
    assert [sample["gt"] for sample in first["samples"]] == ["0/1", "0/1"]
    assert [sample["dp"] for sample in first["samples"]] == [3, 10]
    assert [sample["ad"] for sample in first["samples"]] == [[1, 2], [8, 2]]

    hom = payload[1]
    assert hom["samples"][0]["gt"] == "1/1"
    assert hom["samples"][0]["ad"] == [2, 8]

    insertion = payload[3]
    assert [sample["sample"] for sample in insertion["samples"]] == ["s4", "s5"]
    assert [sample["gt"] for sample in insertion["samples"]] == ["0/1", "1/1"]

    # sample_count, allele_count (1 for 0/1, 2 for 1/1) and total depth.
    assert [row["sample_count"] for row in payload] == [2, 1, 1, 2]
    assert [row["allele_count"] for row in payload] == [2, 2, 1, 3]
    assert [row["depth"] for row in payload] == [13, 10, 4, 7]

    # Only actual callers are listed; the no-variant sample s3 appears
    # nowhere even though it sits between callers in the manifest.
    assert all(
        sample["sample"] != "s3"
        for row in payload
        for sample in row["samples"]
    )

    assert out.endswith("\n") and not out.endswith("\n\n")


def test_same_contract_holds_with_shared_non_default_thresholds(workspace) -> None:
    # min-alt-count 3 drops the heterozygous AC=2 sites; min-base-quality
    # 15 admits the low-quality evidence; the homozygous fraction of 0.7
    # re-genotypes the s4 insertion (3/4) as 1/1.
    extra = [
        "--min-base-quality", "15",
        "--min-alt-count", "3",
        "--min-alt-fraction", "0.3",
        "--homozygous-fraction", "0.7",
        "--call-indels",
    ]
    code_batch, out_batch, err_batch = run_cli(_batch_argv(workspace, *extra))
    assert code_batch == 0 and err_batch == ""
    code_sum, out_sum, err_sum = _call_each_sample_then_summarize(workspace, *extra)
    assert code_sum == 0 and err_sum == ""
    assert out_batch == out_sum

    payload = [json.loads(line) for line in out_batch.splitlines()]
    assert [
        tuple(row[key] for key in ("chrom", "pos", "ref", "alt")) for row in payload
    ] == [
        ("c1", 8, "T", "A"),
        ("c3", 6, "C", "CA"),
    ]
    assert payload[0]["samples"] == [
        {"sample": "s2", "gt": "1/1", "dp": 10, "ad": [2, 8]}
    ]
    assert payload[1]["sample_count"] == 2
    assert [sample["gt"] for sample in payload[1]["samples"]] == ["1/1", "1/1"]
    assert payload[1]["allele_count"] == 4
    assert payload[1]["depth"] == 7


def test_default_snv_mode_does_not_emit_the_indel(workspace) -> None:
    code, out, err = run_cli(_batch_argv(workspace))
    assert code == 0 and err == ""
    payload = [json.loads(line) for line in out.splitlines()]
    assert all(row["chrom"] != "c3" for row in payload)
    assert len(payload) == 3
    # The decomposed path agrees in SNV-only mode too.
    _, out_sum, err_sum = _call_each_sample_then_summarize(workspace)
    assert err_sum == ""
    assert out == out_sum


# -- Relative paths resolve against the manifest directory on both paths ---

def test_relative_manifest_paths_ignore_the_working_directory(
    workspace, monkeypatch
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.chdir("/")
    code_batch, out_batch, err_batch = run_cli(_batch_argv(workspace))
    assert code_batch == 0 and err_batch == ""
    # The decomposed manifest stores "vcfs/<sample>.vcf" relative paths;
    # summarize must resolve them against the manifest directory as well.
    code_sum, out_sum, err_sum = _call_each_sample_then_summarize(workspace)
    assert code_sum == 0 and err_sum == ""
    assert out_batch == out_sum


def test_both_paths_agree_from_an_unrelated_working_directory(
    workspace, monkeypatch
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.chdir(workspace / "vcfs")
    code_batch, out_batch, _ = run_cli(_batch_argv(workspace, "--call-indels"))
    code_sum, out_sum, _ = _call_each_sample_then_summarize(
        workspace, "--call-indels"
    )
    assert code_batch == code_sum == 0
    assert out_batch == out_sum


# -- Empty inputs -----------------------------------------------------------

def test_empty_manifest_gives_empty_output_on_both_paths(workspace) -> None:
    (workspace / "reads.jsonl").write_text("\n  \n\n")
    code_batch, out_batch, err_batch = run_cli(_batch_argv(workspace))
    assert code_batch == 0
    assert out_batch == "" and err_batch == ""

    (workspace / "vcfs.jsonl").write_text("\n  \n\n")
    code_sum, out_sum, err_sum = run_cli(
        [
            "summarize-variants",
            str(workspace / "vcfs.jsonl"),
            "--reference",
            str(workspace / "ref.fa"),
        ]
    )
    assert code_sum == 0
    assert out_sum == "" and err_sum == ""
    assert out_batch == out_sum


def test_all_samples_without_variants_give_empty_output_on_both_paths(
    workspace,
) -> None:
    (workspace / "reads.jsonl").write_text(
        json.dumps({"sample": "s3", "reads": "reads/s3.fq"}) + "\n"
    )
    code_batch, out_batch, err_batch = run_cli(_batch_argv(workspace))
    assert code_batch == 0
    assert out_batch == "" and err_batch == ""

    # Decomposed path: s3's VCF is header-only, and the summary is empty.
    vcf_path = workspace / "vcfs" / "s3.vcf"
    code, out, err = run_cli(
        [
            "call-variants",
            str(workspace / "ref.fa"),
            str(workspace / "reads" / "s3.fq"),
            "--sample-name", "s3",
            "--output", str(vcf_path),
        ]
    )
    assert code == 0 and out == "" and err == ""
    assert vcf_path.read_text().startswith("##fileformat=VCFv4.2\n")
    (workspace / "vcfs.jsonl").write_text(
        json.dumps({"sample": "s3", "vcf": "vcfs/s3.vcf"}) + "\n"
    )
    code_sum, out_sum, err_sum = run_cli(
        [
            "summarize-variants",
            str(workspace / "vcfs.jsonl"),
            "--reference",
            str(workspace / "ref.fa"),
        ]
    )
    assert code_sum == 0
    assert out_sum == "" and err_sum == ""
    assert out_batch == out_sum


# -- A failing later sample fails the whole batch atomically ----------------

def test_corrupt_later_fastq_fails_batch_without_partial_output(
    workspace,
) -> None:
    # A trailing sample (after five valid ones) has a truncated FASTQ.
    (workspace / "reads" / "broken.fq").write_text("@broken\nACGT\n+broken\nII\n")
    manifest = workspace / "reads.jsonl"
    manifest.write_text(
        manifest.read_text()
        + json.dumps({"sample": "s6", "reads": "reads/broken.fq"}) + "\n"
    )
    target = workspace / "out.jsonl"
    target.write_text("PREEXISTING\n")

    code, out, err = run_cli(_batch_argv(workspace, "--output", str(target)))
    assert code == 2
    assert out == ""
    assert err.count("\n") == 1
    # The pre-existing destination is untouched and no temp summary stays.
    assert target.read_text() == "PREEXISTING\n"
    assert list(workspace.glob(".batch-call-variants-*")) == []


def test_corrupt_later_fastq_fails_the_per_sample_call_the_same_way(
    workspace,
) -> None:
    # The decomposed path reaches that read through call-variants: the
    # same malformed input must fail there with the same usage exit code,
    # so batch consistency cannot come from relaxed validation.
    (workspace / "reads" / "broken.fq").write_text("@broken\nACGT\n+broken\nII\n")
    code, out, err = run_cli(
        [
            "call-variants",
            str(workspace / "ref.fa"),
            str(workspace / "reads" / "broken.fq"),
            "--sample-name", "s6",
        ]
    )
    assert code == 2
    assert out == ""
    assert err.count("\n") == 1


# -- Determinism: repetition and physical read chunking ---------------------

def test_repeated_runs_produce_identical_bytes(workspace) -> None:
    argv = _batch_argv(workspace, "--call-indels")
    first = run_cli(argv)
    second = run_cli(argv)
    assert first == second
    assert first[0] == 0 and first[2] == ""
    # And the decomposed path is repeatable as well.
    decomposed_first = _call_each_sample_then_summarize(workspace, "--call-indels")
    decomposed_second = _call_each_sample_then_summarize(workspace, "--call-indels")
    assert decomposed_first == decomposed_second
    assert first[1] == decomposed_first[1]


def _wrapped_fastq_text(records, chunk: int) -> str:
    """Serialize records with sequence/quality wrapped every *chunk* bases.

    The FASTQ reader accumulates wrapped sequence and quality segments
    into the same logical records, so this varies the physical line
    chunking seen during iteration without changing a single record.
    """
    lines: list[str] = []
    for record in records:
        quality = "".join(chr(score + 33) for score in record.quality)
        lines.append("@" + record.identifier)
        for start in range(0, len(record.sequence), chunk):
            lines.append(record.sequence[start : start + chunk])
        lines.append("+" + record.identifier)
        for start in range(0, len(quality), chunk):
            lines.append(quality[start : start + chunk])
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("chunk", [1, 3, 7])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("extra", [[], ["--call-indels"]])
def test_output_is_independent_of_physical_read_chunking(
    workspace, chunk, extra
) -> None:
    # Rewrite every sample FASTQ with its records wrapped across multiple
    # physical lines; logical records, order and thresholds are unchanged.
    wrapped_dir = workspace / "reads_wrapped"
    wrapped_dir.mkdir()

def test_public_exception_types_are_unchanged() -> None:
    """The documented exception types survive on both composition sides."""
    # Invalid thresholds are ValueErrors raised before reads are consumed.
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        batch_call_variants((), REFERENCE_RECORDS, min_base_quality=94)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        call_variants(REFERENCE_RECORDS, (), min_base_quality=94)

    # An empty reference is a VariantCallingError on both sides.
    with pytest.raises(VariantCallingError):
        batch_call_variants((), ())
    with pytest.raises(VariantCallingError):
        call_variants((), ())

    # Malformed manifests keep their entry-specific error types.
    with pytest.raises(BatchManifestError):
        batch_call_variants(StringIO("{not json}\n"), REFERENCE_RECORDS)
    with pytest.raises(ManifestError):
        summarize_variants(StringIO("{not json}\n"), REFERENCE_RECORDS)

    # Missing files keep propagating as OSError.
    with pytest.raises(OSError):
        batch_call_variants("/no/such/manifest.jsonl", REFERENCE_RECORDS)
    with pytest.raises(OSError):
        summarize_variants(
            StringIO('{"sample":"s1","vcf":"/no/such/s1.vcf"}\n'),
            REFERENCE_RECORDS,
        )

1061	def _read_single_record(
1062	    path: str,
1063	    fmt: str,
1064	    parser: argparse.ArgumentParser,
1065	    label: str,
1066	) -> tuple[SequenceRecord | None, object, bool, int]:
1067	    """Read exactly one record from *path*.
1068	
1069	    Returns ``(record, stream, close, exit_code)``; *record* is ``None``
1070	    when the invocation failed and *exit_code* is then ``1`` or ``2``.
1071	    ``"-"`` reads from standard input.
1072	    """
1073	    if path == "-":
1074	        stream = sys.stdin
1075	        close = False
1076	    else:
1077	        try:
1078	            stream = open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", newline="")
1079	        except OSError as exc:
1080	            print(f"{parser.prog}: {label}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
1081	            return None, None, False, 1
1082	        close = True
1083	
1084	    try:
1085	        records = read_sequences(stream, format=fmt)
1086	        try:
1087	            first = next(records)
1088	        except StopIteration:
1089	            raise SequenceFormatError(f"{label}: empty input")
1090	        try:
1091	            next(records)
1092	        except StopIteration:
1093	            return first, stream, close, 0
1094	        raise SequenceFormatError(f"{label}: expected exactly one record, got more")
1095	    except (SequenceFormatError, SequenceValidationError, ValueError) as exc:
1096	        if close:
1097	            stream.close()
1098	        print(f"{parser.prog}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
1099	        return None, None, False, 2
1100	    except OSError as exc:
1101	        if close:
1102	            stream.close()
1103	        print(f"{parser.prog}: {label}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)

"""Command line entry point for genome-variant-toolkit."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import tempfile
from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator, Sequence

from . import __version__
from .alignment import PairwiseAlignment, align_pair
from .annotation import AnnotationFormatError, annotate_vcf
from .batch import BatchManifestError, batch_call_variants
from .calling import VariantCallingError, call_variants
from .comparison import (
    VariantComparisonError,
    compare_variants,
    render_comparison,
)
from .coverage import coverage_report
from .deduplication import deduplicate_reads
from .kmer import build_kmer_index
from .mapping import MappingReferenceError, map_reads
from .quality import ReadQualityError, filter_reads
from .sequence_io import (
    SequenceFormatError,
    SequenceRecord,
    SequenceValidationError,
    read_sequences,
    write_sequences,
)
from .summary import (
    ManifestError,
    render_summaries,
    summarize_variants,
)
from .vcf import (
    ReferenceMismatchError,
    VcfFormatError,
    normalize_vcf,
    read_vcf,
    render_vcf,
)

# Read/parse/processing errors that make the invocation invalid usage.
# ReadQualityError is a ValueError subclass but is listed explicitly.
_READ_ERRORS = (
    SequenceFormatError,
    SequenceValidationError,
    ReadQualityError,
    VcfFormatError,
    ReferenceMismatchError,
    ValueError,
)


def _positive_int(value: str) -> int:
    try:
        parsed = int(value)
    except ValueError:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"{value!r} is not a positive integer")
    if parsed <= 0:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"{value!r} is not a positive integer")
    return parsed


def _quality_int(value: str) -> int:
    try:
        parsed = int(value)
    except ValueError:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            f"{value!r} is not an integer in the range 0-93"
        )
    if not 0 <= parsed <= 93:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            f"{value!r} is not an integer in the range 0-93"
        )
    return parsed


def _nonnegative_int(value: str) -> int:
    try:
        parsed = int(value)
    except ValueError:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            f"{value!r} is not a non-negative integer"
        )
    if parsed < 0:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            f"{value!r} is not a non-negative integer"
        )
    return parsed


def _fraction(value: str) -> float:
    try:
        parsed = float(value)
    except ValueError:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            f"{value!r} is not a number in the range 0-1"
        )
    if not math.isfinite(parsed) or not 0 <= parsed <= 1:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
            f"{value!r} is not a finite number in the range 0-1"
        )
    return parsed


def _prefix(first: SequenceRecord, rest: Iterable[SequenceRecord]) -> Iterator[SequenceRecord]:
    yield first
    yield from rest


class _ArgumentParser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    """Argument parser that reports errors as one line on stderr."""

    def error(self, message: str) -> None:
        sys.stderr.write(f"{self.prog}: error: {message}\n")
        raise SystemExit(2)


def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = _ArgumentParser(
        prog="genome-variant-toolkit",
        description="Genomic variant analysis toolkit from reads to annotated calls",
    )
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command")
    sub.add_parser("version", help="print the current version")

    normalize = sub.add_parser(
        "normalize-sequences",
        help="read FASTA/FASTQ sequences and write them in a normalized form",
    )
    normalize.add_argument("input", help="input file, or '-' for standard input")
    normalize.add_argument(
        "--input-format",
        choices=("fasta", "fastq", "auto"),
        default="auto",
        help="input format (default: auto-detect from the first title line)",
    )
    normalize.add_argument(
        "--output-format",
        choices=("fasta", "fastq", "auto"),
        default="auto",
        help="output format (default: keep the detected input format)",
    )
    normalize.add_argument(
        "--output",
        default="-",
        help="output file, or '-' for standard output (default: standard output)",
    )
    normalize.add_argument(
        "--line-width",
        type=_positive_int,
        default=60,
        help="maximum FASTA sequence line width in characters (default: 60); "
        "FASTQ layout is always four lines per record",
    )

    filter_reads_cmd = sub.add_parser(
        "filter-reads",
        help="trim low-quality ends and filter FASTQ reads",
    )
    filter_reads_cmd.add_argument("input", help="FASTQ input file, or '-' for standard input")
    filter_reads_cmd.add_argument(
        "--min-end-quality",
        type=_quality_int,
        default=20,
        metavar="N",
        help="trim bases with Phred quality strictly below N from both ends "
        "(default: 20)",
    )
    filter_reads_cmd.add_argument(
        "--min-mean-quality",
        type=_quality_int,
        default=20,
        metavar="N",
        help="drop reads whose mean Phred quality is below N after trimming "
        "(default: 20)",
    )
    filter_reads_cmd.add_argument(
        "--min-length",
        type=_positive_int,
        default=30,
        metavar="N",
        help="drop reads shorter than N bases after trimming (default: 30)",
    )
    filter_reads_cmd.add_argument(
        "--output",
        default="-",
        help="output file, or '-' for standard output (default: standard output)",
    )

    dedup_cmd = sub.add_parser(
        "deduplicate-reads",
        help="deduplicate FASTA/FASTQ reads before mapping and variant calling",
    )
    dedup_cmd.add_argument("input", help="input file, or '-' for standard input")
    dedup_cmd.add_argument(
        "--input-format",
        choices=("fasta", "fastq", "auto"),
        default="auto",
        help="input format (default: auto-detect from the first title line)",
    )
    dedup_cmd.add_argument(
        "--canonical",
        action="store_true",
        help="also treat a sequence and its IUPAC reverse complement as "
        "duplicates (default: only identical sequences are grouped)",
    )
    dedup_cmd.add_argument(
        "--output",
        default="-",
        help="output file, or '-' for standard output (default: standard output)",
    )

    kmer_index_cmd = sub.add_parser(
        "kmer-index",
        help="build a k-mer index and write it as JSON Lines",
    )
    kmer_index_cmd.add_argument("input", help="input file, or '-' for standard input")
    kmer_index_cmd.add_argument(
        "--input-format",
        choices=("fasta", "fastq", "auto"),
        default="auto",
        help="input format (default: auto-detect from the first title line)",
    )
    kmer_index_cmd.add_argument(
        "--k",
        type=_positive_int,
        required=True,
        metavar="N",
        help="k-mer length (a positive integer)",
    )
    kmer_index_cmd.add_argument(
        "--no-canonical",
        action="store_true",
        help="index k-mers on the forward strand only (default: canonicalize "
        "each k-mer against its reverse complement)",
    )
    kmer_index_cmd.add_argument(
        "--output",
        default="-",
        help="output file, or '-' for standard output (default: standard output)",
    )

    align_pair_cmd = sub.add_parser(
        "align-pair",
        help="align two single-record FASTA/FASTQ inputs pairwise",
    )
    align_pair_cmd.add_argument(
        "reference", help="reference input file, or '-' for standard input"
    )
    align_pair_cmd.add_argument(
        "query", help="query input file, or '-' for standard input"
    )
    align_pair_cmd.add_argument(
        "--reference-format",
        choices=("fasta", "fastq", "auto"),
        default="auto",
        help="reference input format (default: auto-detect)",
    )
    align_pair_cmd.add_argument(
        "--query-format",
        choices=("fasta", "fastq", "auto"),
        default="auto",
        help="query input format (default: auto-detect)",
    )
    align_pair_cmd.add_argument(
        "--mode",
        choices=("global", "local"),
        default="global",
        help="alignment mode (default: global)",
    )
    align_pair_cmd.add_argument(
        "--match",
        "--match-score",
        dest="match",
        type=_positive_int,
        default=2,
        metavar="N",
        help="match score, a positive integer (default: 2)",
    )
    align_pair_cmd.add_argument(
        "--mismatch",
        "--mismatch-penalty",
        dest="mismatch",
        type=_nonnegative_int,
        default=3,
        metavar="N",
        help="mismatch penalty, a non-negative integer (default: 3)",
    )
    align_pair_cmd.add_argument(
        "--gap-open",
        type=_nonnegative_int,
        default=5,
        metavar="N",
        help="gap opening penalty, a non-negative integer (default: 5)",
    )
    align_pair_cmd.add_argument(
        "--gap-extend",
        type=_nonnegative_int,
        default=2,
        metavar="N",
        help="gap extension penalty, a non-negative integer (default: 2)",
    )
    align_pair_cmd.add_argument(
        "--output",
        default="-",
        help="output file, or '-' for standard output (default: standard output)",
    )

    normalize_vcf_cmd = sub.add_parser(
        "normalize-vcf",
        help="normalize VCF variants against a reference FASTA",
    )
    normalize_vcf_cmd.add_argument(
        "input", help="VCF input file, or '-' for standard input"
    )
    normalize_vcf_cmd.add_argument(
        "--reference",
        required=True,
        help="reference FASTA file (required); '-' denotes standard input",
    )
    normalize_vcf_cmd.add_argument(
        "--output",
        default="-",
        help="output file, or '-' for standard output (default: standard output)",
    )

    annotate_vcf_cmd = sub.add_parser(
        "annotate-vcf",
        help="annotate VCF SNVs and short ACGT indels against a "
        "reference FASTA and GFF3 features",
    )
    annotate_vcf_cmd.add_argument(
        "input", help="VCF input file, or '-' for standard input"
    )
    annotate_vcf_cmd.add_argument(
        "--reference",
        required=True,
        help="reference FASTA file (required); '-' denotes standard input",
    )
    annotate_vcf_cmd.add_argument(
        "--features",
        required=True,
        help="GFF3 feature file (required); '-' denotes standard input",
    )
    annotate_vcf_cmd.add_argument(
        "--output",
        default="-",
        help="output file, or '-' for standard output (default: standard output)",
    )

    map_reads_cmd = sub.add_parser(
        "map-reads",
        help="map FASTA/FASTQ reads against a multi-record FASTA reference",
    )
    map_reads_cmd.add_argument(
        "reference", help="reference FASTA file, or '-' for standard input"
    )
    map_reads_cmd.add_argument(
        "reads", help="reads FASTA/FASTQ file, or '-' for standard input"
    )
    map_reads_cmd.add_argument(
        "--reads-format",
